challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: The infrastructure bill has doubled, and we are not absorbing that increase. I am cutting the automated drift monitoring budget to zero. This is a hard line. As long as our infrastructure spend remains above the current baseline, I will not fund any new automation for drift checks. We will rely on the existing manual reviews for now. Do not bring this back to me until the cost structure is resolved. I am not willing to pay for luxury tooling while our core replenishment costs are out of control. The decision is final for this quarter.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines a threshold (infrastructure spend above baseline) and a specific refusal (no funding for new automation) that constitutes a line whose crossing is unacceptable to the author.
